title: Chapter6
description: Finnish vocabulary: weather, seasons, clothing, nature and verbs

questions.question: To drive
questions.explanation: 'Ajaa' (type 1 verb) means to drive; 'ajan' is 'I drive'.
questions.exampletranslate: I drive to work by car.

questions.question: Down / Downstairs
questions.explanation: 'Alhaalla' means down or downstairs; 'alhaalta' is 'from below'.
questions.exampletranslate: I am downstairs in the kitchen.

questions.question: Under
questions.explanation: 'Alla' means under (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The cat is under the table.

questions.question: To start
questions.explanation: 'Aloittaa' (type 1 verb) means to start; 'aloitan' is 'I start'.
questions.exampletranslate: I start a new hobby.

questions.question: Degree
questions.explanation: 'Aste' means degree (e.g. temperature); its genitive is 'asteen'.
questions.exampletranslate: It is ten degrees outside.

questions.question: Sun
questions.explanation: 'Aurinko' means sun; its genitive is 'auringon'.
questions.exampletranslate: The sun is shining today.

questions.question: In front of
questions.explanation: 'Edessä' means in front of (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The car is in front of the house.

questions.question: Yesterday
questions.explanation: 'Eilen' means yesterday.
questions.exampletranslate: Yesterday it snowed.

questions.question: Record (best result)
questions.explanation: 'Ennätys' means record (e.g. a best result); its genitive is 'ennätyksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: He set a new record.

questions.question: First snow
questions.explanation: 'Ensilumi' means the first snow of the season; its genitive is 'ensilumen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The first snow came in October.

questions.question: To search
questions.explanation: 'Etsiä' (type 1 verb) means to search; 'etsin' is 'I search' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I am looking for a new jacket.

questions.question: Overalls / Coveralls
questions.explanation: 'Haalarit' means overalls or coveralls (a plural word); its genitive is 'haalarien'.
questions.exampletranslate: The child puts on overalls to go out.

questions.question: To fetch / apply for
questions.explanation: 'Hakea' (type 1 verb) means to fetch, get or apply for; 'haen' is 'I fetch'.
questions.exampletranslate: I pick up the child from daycare.

questions.question: Skirt
questions.explanation: 'Hame' means skirt; its genitive is 'hameen'.
questions.exampletranslate: She puts on a beautiful skirt.

questions.question: Hobby
questions.explanation: 'Harrastus' means hobby; its genitive is 'harrastuksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: Swimming is my hobby.

questions.question: Pea
questions.explanation: 'Herne' means pea; its genitive is 'herneen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I make pea soup.

questions.question: To ski
questions.explanation: 'Hiihtää' (type 1 verb) means to ski (cross-country); 'hiihdän' is 'I ski'.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter I ski in the forest.

questions.question: Lift / Elevator
questions.explanation: 'Hissi' means lift or elevator.
questions.exampletranslate: I take the lift to the fifth floor.

questions.question: Trousers / Pants
questions.explanation: 'Housut' means trousers or pants (a plural word); its genitive is 'housujen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy new trousers.

questions.question: Tomorrow
questions.explanation: 'Huomenna' means tomorrow.
questions.exampletranslate: Tomorrow it will snow.

questions.question: In a good mood
questions.explanation: 'Hyvällä tuulella' means in a good mood.
questions.exampletranslate: I am in a good mood today.

questions.question: In the evening
questions.explanation: 'Illalla' means in the evening.
questions.exampletranslate: In the evening I watch the program.

questions.question: Without
questions.explanation: 'Ilman' means without (used with the partitive).
questions.exampletranslate: I go out without a jacket.

questions.question: To do yoga
questions.explanation: 'Joogata' (type 4 verb) means to do yoga; 'joogaan' is 'I do yoga'.
questions.exampletranslate: I do yoga every morning.

questions.question: To celebrate
questions.explanation: 'Juhlia' (type 1 verb) means to celebrate; 'juhlin' is 'I celebrate'.
questions.exampletranslate: We celebrate a birthday.

questions.question: Story / Thing / Matter
questions.explanation: 'Juttu' means story, thing or matter (informal); its genitive is 'jutun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I'll tell you a funny story.

questions.question: To fish
questions.explanation: 'Kalastaa' (type 1 verb) means to fish; 'kalastan' is 'I fish'.
questions.exampletranslate: I fish on the lake in summer.

questions.question: Street level
questions.explanation: 'Katutaso' means street level.
questions.exampletranslate: The shop is at street level.

questions.question: Summer
questions.explanation: 'Kesä' means summer.
questions.exampletranslate: In summer it is warm.

questions.question: Ketchup
questions.explanation: 'Ketsuppi' means ketchup; its genitive is 'ketsupin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I put ketchup on the fries.

questions.question: Spring
questions.explanation: 'Kevät' means spring; its genitive is 'kevään'.
questions.exampletranslate: In spring the snow melts.

questions.question: Size
questions.explanation: 'Koko' means size (it can also mean whole or all); its genitive is 'koon'.
questions.exampletranslate: What is your size?

questions.question: Homeland / Home country
questions.explanation: 'Kotimaa' means homeland or home country.
questions.exampletranslate: My home country is Turkey.

questions.question: Rubber boots
questions.explanation: 'Kumisaappaat' means rubber boots (a plural word); its genitive is 'kumisaappaiden'.
questions.exampletranslate: In the rain I wear rubber boots.

questions.question: Rain / mud pants
questions.explanation: 'Kurahousut' means rain or mud trousers (a plural word); its genitive is 'kurahousujen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The child has rain pants on.

questions.question: To knit
questions.explanation: 'Kutoa' (type 1 verb) means to knit; 'kudon' is 'I knit'.
questions.exampletranslate: I knit a wool sweater for winter.

questions.question: Gift
questions.explanation: 'Lahja' means gift.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a gift for a friend.

questions.question: Mittens
questions.explanation: 'Lapaset' means mittens (a plural word); its genitive is 'lapasten'.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter I wear mittens.

questions.question: Lapland
questions.explanation: 'Lappi' means Lapland; its genitive is 'Lapin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I travel to Lapland in winter.

questions.question: To go down / set (the sun)
questions.explanation: 'Laskea' (type 1 verb) means to go down, count or set; 'aurinko laskee' means 'the sun sets'.
questions.exampletranslate: The sun sets in the evening.

questions.question: Nickname
questions.explanation: 'Lempinimi' means nickname; its genitive is 'lempinimen'.
questions.exampletranslate: His nickname is Make.

questions.question: Too much
questions.explanation: 'Liika' means too much or excess; 'liian' is the adverb 'too'.
questions.exampletranslate: This is too much.

questions.question: Dirty
questions.explanation: 'Likainen' means dirty; its genitive is 'likaisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The clothes are dirty.

questions.question: List
questions.explanation: 'Lista' means list.
questions.exampletranslate: I make a shopping list.

questions.question: To end / run out
questions.explanation: 'Loppua' (type 1 verb) means to end or run out; 'se loppuu' means 'it ends'.
questions.exampletranslate: The summer holiday ends soon.

questions.question: Snow
questions.explanation: 'Lumi' means snow; its genitive is 'lumen'.
questions.exampletranslate: There is a lot of snow in the yard.

questions.question: To snowboard
questions.explanation: 'Lumilautailla' (type 3 verb) means to snowboard; 'lumilautailen' is 'I snowboard'.
questions.exampletranslate: I snowboard in Lapland.

questions.question: Nature
questions.explanation: 'Luonto' means nature; its genitive is 'luonnon'.
questions.exampletranslate: I love Finnish nature.

questions.question: To trust
questions.explanation: 'Luottaa' (type 1 verb) means to trust; 'luotan' is 'I trust' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I trust you.

questions.question: To think / suppose
questions.explanation: 'Luulla' (type 1 verb) means to think or suppose; 'luulen' is 'I think/suppose'.
questions.exampletranslate: I think it will rain tomorrow.

questions.question: Near
questions.explanation: 'Lähellä' means near or nearby.
questions.exampletranslate: The shop is near.

questions.question: Thermometer
questions.explanation: 'Lämpömittari' means thermometer, from 'lämpö' (heat) and 'mittari' (gauge).
questions.exampletranslate: The thermometer shows five degrees.

questions.question: To find
questions.explanation: 'Löytää' (type 1 verb) means to find; 'löydän' is 'I find'.
questions.exampletranslate: I find the keys in the bag.

questions.question: Strawberry
questions.explanation: 'Mansikka' means strawberry; its genitive is 'mansikan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I eat strawberries in summer.

questions.question: To travel
questions.explanation: 'Matkustaa' (type 1 verb) means to travel; 'matkustan' is 'I travel'.
questions.exampletranslate: I travel to Lapland by train.

questions.question: Fashion
questions.explanation: 'Muoti' means fashion; its genitive is 'muodin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I follow fashion.

questions.question: Amount / Quantity
questions.explanation: 'Määrä' means amount or quantity.
questions.exampletranslate: The amount of snow is large.

questions.question: Cottage
questions.explanation: 'Mökki' means cottage; its genitive is 'mökin'.
questions.exampletranslate: In summer we go to the cottage.

questions.question: To look (like)
questions.explanation: 'Näyttää' (type 1 verb) means to look (like) or show; 'näytän' is 'I look/show' (used with 'miltä').
questions.exampletranslate: This jacket looks good.

questions.question: Program
questions.explanation: 'Ohjelma' means program.
questions.exampletranslate: I watch a good program.

questions.question: To sew
questions.explanation: 'Ommella' means to sew; 'ompelen' is 'I sew'.
questions.exampletranslate: I sew a button onto the shirt.

questions.question: To sunbathe (take in the sun)
questions.explanation: 'Ottaa aurinkoa' means to sunbathe; 'otan aurinkoa' is 'I sunbathe'.
questions.exampletranslate: I sunbathe on the beach.

questions.question: To shine / fry
questions.explanation: 'Paistaa' (type 1 verb) means to shine (sun) or to fry; 'paistan' is 'I shine/fry'.
questions.exampletranslate: The sun shines brightly.

questions.question: Shirt
questions.explanation: 'Paita' means shirt; its genitive is 'paidan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I dress in a white shirt.

questions.question: Frost / Freezing cold
questions.explanation: 'Pakkanen' means frost or freezing weather; its genitive is 'pakkasen'.
questions.exampletranslate: It is freezing cold outside.

questions.question: Bank
questions.explanation: 'Pankki' means bank; its genitive is 'pankin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I am going to the bank.

questions.question: Mirror
questions.explanation: 'Peili' means mirror.
questions.exampletranslate: I look at myself in the mirror.

questions.question: Dark
questions.explanation: 'Pimeä' means dark.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter it is dark.

questions.question: Beanie / Woolly hat
questions.explanation: 'Pipo' means beanie or woolly hat.
questions.exampletranslate: In the cold I wear a beanie.

questions.question: To fall
questions.explanation: 'Pudota' (type 4 verb) means to fall; 'putoan' is 'I fall'.
questions.exampletranslate: The leaves fall in autumn.

questions.question: To put on / dress
questions.explanation: 'Pukea' (type 1 verb) means to put on or dress; 'puen päälle' means 'I put on'.
questions.exampletranslate: I put the jacket on.

questions.question: Sweater / Blouse
questions.explanation: 'Pusero' means a sweater or blouse.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a warm sweater.

questions.question: Tree
questions.explanation: 'Puu' means tree (also wood); its genitive is 'puun'.
questions.exampletranslate: There is a big tree in the garden.

questions.question: Garden
questions.explanation: 'Puutarha' means garden.
questions.exampletranslate: I grow flowers in the garden.

questions.question: On top of
questions.explanation: 'Päällä' means on top of (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The book is on top of the table.

questions.question: Tires
questions.explanation: 'Renkaat' means tires (a plural word); its genitive is 'renkaiden'.
questions.exampletranslate: I change the winter tires on the car.

questions.question: Boots
questions.explanation: 'Saappaat' means boots (a plural word); its genitive is 'saappaiden'.
questions.exampletranslate: I put on warm boots.

questions.question: To rain / snow (precipitate)
questions.explanation: 'Sataa' (type 1 verb) means to rain or snow (to precipitate); 'sataa' is 'it rains/snows'.
questions.exampletranslate: It is snowing outside.

questions.question: To stand
questions.explanation: 'Seisoa' (type 1 verb) means to stand; 'seison' is 'I stand'.
questions.exampletranslate: I stand in the queue.

questions.question: To fit / agree
questions.explanation: 'Sopia' (type 1 verb) means to fit, suit or agree; 'sovin' is 'I agree/it fits'.
questions.exampletranslate: This jacket fits me.

questions.question: Suitable
questions.explanation: 'Sopiva' means suitable.
questions.exampletranslate: This is a suitable size.

questions.question: Gloves (fingered)
questions.explanation: 'Sormikkaat' means gloves with fingers (a plural word); its genitive is 'sormikkaiden'.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter I wear gloves.

questions.question: To try on (clothes)
questions.explanation: 'Sovittaa' (type 1 verb) means to try on; 'sovitan' is 'I try on' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I try on the jacket at the shop.

questions.question: Fitting room
questions.explanation: 'Sovituskoppi' means fitting room; its genitive is 'sovituskopin'.
questions.exampletranslate: Clothes are tried on in the fitting room.

questions.question: Autumn
questions.explanation: 'Syksy' means autumn.
questions.exampletranslate: In autumn it often rains.

questions.question: Weather
questions.explanation: 'Sää' means weather; its genitive is 'sään'.
questions.exampletranslate: What kind of weather is it today?

questions.question: To save
questions.explanation: 'Säästää' (type 1 verb) means to save (money or resources); 'säästän' is 'I save'.
questions.exampletranslate: I save money for a holiday.

questions.question: Behind
questions.explanation: 'Takana' means behind (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The garden is behind the house.

questions.question: Jacket / Coat
questions.explanation: 'Takki' means jacket or coat; its genitive is 'takin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I put on the jacket.

questions.question: Winter
questions.explanation: 'Talvi' means winter; its genitive is 'talven'.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter it is cold.

questions.question: Winter jacket
questions.explanation: 'Talvitakki' means winter jacket; its genitive is 'talvitakin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a warm winter jacket.

questions.question: To text
questions.explanation: 'Tekstata' (type 4 verb) means to text (send a text message); 'tekstaan' is 'I text'.
questions.exampletranslate: I text a friend.

questions.question: Order (purchase order)
questions.explanation: 'Tilaus' means order (e.g. a purchase order); its genitive is 'tilauksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The order arrives next week.

questions.question: Product
questions.explanation: 'Tuote' means product; its genitive is 'tuotteen'.
questions.exampletranslate: This product is cheap.

questions.question: T-shirt
questions.explanation: 'T-paita' means t-shirt.
questions.exampletranslate: In summer I wear a t-shirt.

questions.question: Fire
questions.explanation: 'Tuli' means fire; its genitive is 'tulen'.
questions.exampletranslate: A fire burns in the fireplace.

questions.question: To be windy
questions.explanation: 'Tuulla' (type 1 verb) means to be windy; 'tuulee' means 'it is windy'.
questions.exampletranslate: It is very windy outside.

questions.question: Thunderstorm
questions.explanation: 'Ukkonen' means thunderstorm; its genitive is 'ukkosen'.
questions.exampletranslate: In summer there are often thunderstorms.

questions.question: Although / Even if
questions.explanation: 'Vaikka' means although or even if.
questions.exampletranslate: I go out, even though it rains.

questions.question: To choose
questions.explanation: 'Valita' (type 4 verb) means to choose; 'valitsen' is 'I choose'.
questions.exampletranslate: I choose the blue jacket.

questions.question: Bright / Light
questions.explanation: 'Valoisa' means bright or full of light.
questions.exampletranslate: The apartment is bright.

questions.question: Storage / Warehouse
questions.explanation: 'Varasto' means storage or warehouse.
questions.exampletranslate: The product is out of stock in the warehouse.

questions.question: Opposite
questions.explanation: 'Vastakohta' means opposite; its genitive is 'vastakohdan'.
questions.exampletranslate: Hot is the opposite of cold.

questions.question: Next to
questions.explanation: 'Vieressä' means next to or beside (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The bank is next to the shop.

questions.question: Wool sweater
questions.explanation: 'Villapaita' means wool sweater, from 'villa' (wool) and 'paita' (shirt); its genitive is 'villapaidan'.
questions.exampletranslate: In winter I wear a wool sweater.

questions.question: Seasons
questions.explanation: 'Vuodenajat' means the seasons of the year (a plural word).
questions.exampletranslate: In Finland there are four seasons.

questions.question: Up / Upstairs
questions.explanation: 'Ylhäällä' means up or upstairs; 'ylhäältä' is 'from above'.
questions.exampletranslate: The bedroom is upstairs.
